source: NWS NDFD (graphical.weather.gov ndfdXMLclient.php, time-series) and Open-Meteo (api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast), a 3x2 lattice over 121W-117W, 31N-33N: San Diego's coast and the sea west of it

traps.ndfd-days.xml: offshore points (121W, 119W) answer nil; after 20:00 local the first maximum is tomorrow's
traps.ndfd-hour.xml: begin sent with its Z; without it NDFD reads the hour as each point's local time
traps.ndfd-days-wind.xml: captured 2026-09-27T17:39Z with wspd and wdir: hourly sustained wind in knots, its first hour the next hour
traps.openmeteo-wind.json: captured 2026-09-27T17:39Z with wind: hourly km/h and degrees, each day's peak and dominant direction
traps.openmeteo.json: every point answered, the sea included; hours in each point's local time with its offset
traps.openmeteo-rain-days.json: captured 2026-09-27T21:35Z over south-east Alaska (135W-131W, 57N-59N): its points in two zones, Alaska's and British Columbia's an hour apart, so each day's heaviest hour is read on the point's own date; rain and showers apart, snowfall in cm
traps.openmeteo-rain-hours.json: captured 2026-09-27T21:35Z, forecast_hours=4: the current hour first, in each point's zone
